name: Blender
summary: A general-purpose 3D content creation application that stores editable scenes as structured data-blocks, evaluates dependency relations through a dependency graph, and exposes multiple editor and rendering boundaries.

features.name: Scene, collection, and data-block model
features.description: Blender's fixed DNA scene types represent scenes, view layers, collections, and objects as structured persistent data. Objects reference separate data-block families such as meshes, cameras, and lights, allowing editable content to be shared and linked rather than embedded in one monolithic scene record.
benefits: Separates reusable content data from object placement and scene membership
Supports linked and layered organization of complex projects
costs: Indirection across data-block relationships increases lifecycle complexity
Users and tools must preserve consistency between linked collections, objects, and data

features.name: Dependency graph evaluation
features.description: The dependency graph API models relations between original IDs and evaluated copies, and exposes graph evaluation and update operations. This creates a derived evaluation boundary between editable source data and the state consumed by view and render systems.
benefits: Makes derived state and dependency-driven updates explicit
Allows consumers to request evaluated data without replacing editable originals
costs: Evaluation introduces synchronization and invalidation work
Tools must distinguish original data from evaluated copies

features.name: Editor, operator, and data boundaries
features.description: Blender separates persistent scene data from editor spaces and operators that act on context. The documented Python API exposes data access, operators, and context as distinct surfaces, while the source tree places editors, window management, and kernel data APIs in separate subsystems.
benefits: Allows multiple editors and automation paths to act on shared scene data
Keeps UI context and persistent content conceptually distinct
costs: Operator behavior can depend on active context and selection state
Automation must coordinate UI-independent data APIs with context-sensitive operators

features.name: Pluggable render-engine boundary
features.description: Scene settings contain render-engine selection and render configuration, while the manual presents render engines as selectable systems with different capabilities. Render configuration is therefore a scene-level contract consumed by a chosen engine rather than a single fixed renderer implementation.
benefits: Permits different render strategies to consume common scene content
Keeps engine-specific settings visible at the scene configuration boundary
costs: Projects must account for capability and output differences between engines

mathematical_views.question: How do scenes, collections, objects, and data-blocks compose into a persistent editable content graph?
assumptions: Nodes represent typed Blender IDs or scene containers
Edges represent ownership, membership, or data references
The model abstracts file serialization and UI presentation

mathematical_views.question: When does an editable scene relation produce evaluated state available to view and render consumers?
assumptions: Original IDs and evaluated copies are distinct state classes
Relations and updates trigger graph evaluation transitions
The model abstracts scheduler implementation and modifier-specific algorithms

mathematical_views.question: Which scene content and settings can be consumed by a selected render engine without losing required properties?
assumptions: A scene has a selected engine and engine-specific settings
Each engine supports a subset and interpretation of scene properties
Compatibility is a candidate model and does not claim equal output across engines

benefits: Reusable, linkable content with explicit scene organization
costs: Reference-rich data lifecycles are harder to reason about than a flat scene

benefits: Derived state can be evaluated from explicit dependencies
costs: Invalidation and evaluated-copy boundaries add memory and synchronization cost

benefits: Shared content can be manipulated by editors, scripts, and operators
costs: Context-sensitive operations increase automation and reproducibility constraints

benefits: One project model can target multiple rendering strategies
costs: Engine-specific behavior and settings limit portable guarantees
